messages:
jun.park: deploybot bumped this to blocked: promote to prod failed with digest mismatch on registry side. seen in CI for canary-2026.

deploy-bot: Promotion blocked: target digest differs from expected. Source image: gcr/redwood/canary:2026-04-06. Registry error: layer tar mtime changed -> image manifest digest mismatch.

ben.turner: Ugh, this smells like non-reproducible image builds (mtimes in tar). Any recent change to our builder or baseimage?

carla.rossi: No intentional change. We did upgrade buildkit last week on the runners (bk 0.12.1 -> 0.13.0). Could impact tar metadata.

emily.zhao: CI logs show docker save -> registry push step produced different digest than the build artifact we uploaded to our artifact store. Quick snippet: ```sha256:expected=sha256:abcd1234 actual=sha256:efgh5678 layer0:mtime=2026-04-06T12:34:56Z vs 2026-04-06T12:34:57Z```

leo.martin: Are these difference-by-1s mtime changes or actual content differences? If only mtimes, we can rewrite tar with normalized mtimes and repush.

carla.rossi: I ran `tar --mtime='1970-01-01'` locally and got reproducible digest; buildkit seems to preserve mtimes when squashing layers. That would explain it.

ben.turner: What's the risk if we force-promote the current pushed image (override digest check)?

jun.park: Risk: if artifact in artifact-store != registry image, customer's canary traffic would reference a different binary than was evaluated. We can't do that without re-eval. Also breaks accountability.

dave.ng: Operational plan options: 1) repush the image with normalized mtimes and promote; 2) pin runners/buildkit to previous version until we fix reproducibility; 3) rollback canary to last known-good image while we fix. Thoughts?

emily.zhao: Option 1 is fast. I can add a CI step to normalize mtimes on the image tar and re-push within 30 mins. Need a deploy window for promotion though.

leo.martin: Option 2 protects future builds, but we need a long-term fix anyway (reproducible builds). We should do 1+3 short term: repush normalized image and hold promotion to change window, and rollback canary to previous if risk is high.

carla.rossi: Agree. I'll prepare a repush artifact with `docker save | tar --mtime='UTC' --sort=name | gcrane push` and include a checksum step in CI.

ben.turner: Let's avoid emergency force-promote. Also tag the repushed image with both the same tag and a -normalized suffix so we can verify in the console.

jun.park: Action items: Carla to repush with normalized mtimes (ETA 30m), Emily to add quick checksum step in CI to compare artifact-store vs registry (ETA 2h), Dave to schedule a change window for safe promotion (tomorrow 04:00-05:00 UTC) unless we need earlier rollback. If canary still has traffic issues, roll back to canary@sha256:prevgood.

deploy-bot: Noted. Promotion remains blocked until manifest digests match or manual override is set by @jun.park.

dave.ng: I'll prep rollback runbook now: commands, monitoring checks, and short SLAs for rollback. Putting a hold on promotions in the console.

emily.zhao: Quick CI patch: add `gcrane digest` compare after push and fail if mismatch. I'll open a PR and tag @carla.rossi for verification.

carla.rossi: PR review incoming. I will also add a checkbox to release notes about builder versions and reproducibility so we don't miss this next time.

ben.turner: +1. Also let's add a Canary-guard in the rollout policy: require artifact-store checksum match before traffic shift.

jun.park: Good. If anyone sees pressure to force-promote, escalate to me and @ben.turner. We'll avoid manual overrides unless confirmed. Thanks all.

leo.martin: small note: tag this incident in the release channels and add the logs to the release ticket (TICKET-5432).

jun.park: will do. Closing loop: repush in progress, promotion blocked, change window tomorrow 04:00-05:00 UTC. If repush succeeds and checksum verifies, we'll promote during the window.

deploy-bot: Promotion still blocked. CI artifacts differ: manifest mismatch. Will re-evaluate after CI checksum step passes.
